query: For the paper "Different Absorption from the Same Sharing: Sifted Multi-task Learning for Fake News Detection" (arXiv: 1909.01720), answer this question: Do they report results only on English data?

drafts: Partial: The paper reports experimental results on the RumourEval and PHEME datasets [10][17], and no results on other datasets appear in the supplied passages. However, the passages do not explicitly state the language of these datasets, so whether the reported results are only on English data cannot be confirmed from the provided text. RumourEval contains 325 Twitter threads and PHEME includes 6,425 Twitter threads [17], but no explicit language specification is given.

cited_sources.text: Table 3 provides the experimental results of these methods on RumourEval and PHEME datasets. We have the following observations: • Effectiveness of multi-task learning. MT-trans boosts about 9% and 15% performance im- provements in accuracy on both datasets com- pared with Single-task, which indicates that the multi-task learning method is effective to detect fake news. • Effectiveness of transformer encoder.

Distribution. RumourEval con- tains 325 Twitter threads discussing rumours and PHEME includes 6,425 Twitter threads. Threads, (8) tweets, and class distribution of the two datasets are shown in Table 1. In consideration of the imbalance label distribu- tions, in addition to accuracy (A) metric, we add Precision (P), Recall (R) and F1-score (F1) as com- plementary evaluation metrics for tasks.
